title: Memory allocation guardrails for fair KV eviction and continuous batching
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Production traces show intermittent OOMs and degraded tail latency when mixed tenant workloads trigger continuous batching and large prefix KV cache growth. Root cause analysis points to uncoordinated memory accounting across weights, KV slots, and activations, and lack of soft budget enforcement for low-priority tenants. Goal: implement a lightweight, predictable memory budgeting layer that enforces headroom reservations, enables per-tenant soft quotas, and provides eviction/compaction policies harmonized with the continuous batcher to avoid amplification of tail latency and unexpected weight/activation preemptions.

Scope: (1) a runtime guardrail that tracks three memory pools (weights read-only, KV cache, activation working set) and exposes a single headroom token counter used by scheduling and offload decisions; (2) a prioritized KV eviction policy with age/size/usage signals and tenant-aware fairness; (3) an integration surface for the continuous batcher to respect memory headroom before accepting additional requests; (4) a simulation harness to validate policies at scale and a rollout plan with staged canaries and throttles.

Non-goals: full multi-GPU weight eviction or shard-level model surgery in this ticket (deferred to follow-ups). Long-term model compression work is out of scope but we add hooks to enable it later.
acceptance_criteria: 95% reduction in severity-3 OOM incidents attributable to KV growth on the canary cluster compared to baseline (30-day window)
No more than 3% increase in median latency; 50th/95th/99th tail latency must be within SLO guardrails on canary workloads
Per-tenant soft quota enforcement prevents any single tenant from consuming >X% above their reserved headroom without downgrade or throttling policy (configurable)
Automated simulation reproduces edge-case burst where KV growth + continuous batching would previously trigger OOM; new guardrail prevents OOM in simulation runs
Feature gate and rollout plan with ability to disable on per-cluster basis; monitoring dashboards capturing memory breakdown across weights/KV/activations
implementation_notes: Introduce lightweight MemoryBudget abstraction: atomic counters for weights_readonly, kv_cache_live, activations_live. A derived headroom = total_gpu_mem - sum(counters) - reserved_system_margin.

Soft quotas: per-tenant soft_kv_quota + burst_credit. When tenant exceeds soft_quota for >T seconds, mark as 'bursting' and apply eviction preference and request rejection/degardation depending on policy.

KV eviction ranking: calculate score = alpha*idle_duration_norm + beta*last_access_freq_norm + gamma*tenant_penalty. Evict lowest score first. Where tenant_penalty increases for tenants over soft_quota.

Adaptive compression: when headroom < low_watermark, opportunistically compress less-recent KV slabs with fast LZ4-style codec to reclaim temporary space (configurable, non-blocking), and schedule async decompression on access.

Batcher integration: the continuous batcher must query MemoryBudget.headroom_estimate(tokenized_estimated_tokens) before forming batches larger than N tokens. If insufficient headroom, batcher reduces batch size or stalls low-priority requests.

Headroom sensor: 95th-percentile surge estimator using EWMA over recent allocation deltas with an adjustable smoothing factor and min-guard margin. Expose metric headroom_forecast_95 and headroom_instant.
Testing harness: extend existing memory-simulator to run mixed-tenant traces with variable prefix lengths and simultaneous batching; include deterministic replay for regression detection.
Config surface: cluster-level defaults + per-tenant overrides; control knobs include soft_quota, burst_window_secs, low_watermark_pct, compression_enabled, eviction_weights (alpha/beta/gamma).
Telemetry: add per-eviction telemetry (evicted_bytes, reason, tenant, pre_eviction_headroom) and per-batch headroom checks to existing consoles.
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Created ticket after incidents during mixed-tenant nightly stress tests. Initial spike analysis attached to links below.
2026-02-24: Prototype MemoryBudget counters implemented in dev runtime. Basic headroom calculation validated on unit tests.
2026-02-26: Simulation harness extended with three synthetic tenants (small/medium/large) and continuous-batcher model. Baseline reproduces OOM in ~1/10 runs.
2026-02-28: Implemented tenant-aware eviction ranking; local sim prevents OOM in baseline runs but increases occasional tail latency — tuning in progress.
2026-03-02: Opened PR for soft quota enforcement and batcher-check hook. Need design review for eviction weights and compression trade-offs. Canary rollout plan drafted.
review_feedback: Priya Nair (PM): Favor soft quotas + gradual throttling over hard rejections to preserve PLG UX. Request adding audit log entries for any tenant degradation events.
Nikhil Shah (Infra): Headroom sensor should expose both forecast and raw deltas for debugging. Suggest exposing a debug-only 'memory-claim' trace to correlate allocations to request IDs.
Riya Patel (Reliability): Compression on cold KV slabs ok but ensure async decompression doesn't penalize p95. Add circuit-breaker for compression-induced latency anomalies.
Karin Lopez (Security): Confirm compression buffers cannot be used to leak sensitive state; recommend review by security if hooks use non-zero-copy buffers.
